whatItDoes: Increase the county lodging tax from 2% to 6% for paid lodging stays shorter than 30 consecutive days beginning January 1, 2027. Georgetown is excluded because it has its own lodging tax. The question authorizes $800,000 annually starting in 2027 and whatever amounts are raised in later years, with no stated end date. It also changes how revenue from the full 6% tax would be allocated, as described below. All spending would be subject to an annual independent audit and local government budget laws. Tax revenue could be collected and spent outside the stated constitutional and other legal limits.
yesMeans: Approve the lodging-tax increase, the new allocations for all revenue from the 6% tax, the annual audit requirement and its revenue-limit exception.
noMeans: Do not approve this lodging-tax increase, allocation change or proposed revenue-limit exception.

parts.label: How the revenue would be divided
parts.what: Up to 60% would go to public infrastructure maintenance or improvements and public-safety measures combined. At least 20% would go to childcare, at least 10% to housing, and at least 10% to advertising and marketing local tourism. Childcare and housing could serve tourism-related workers, including seasonal workers, and other workers in the community.

whatItDoes: Increase the county lodging tax from 2% to 5% beginning January 1, 2027, excluding Cortez, which has its own lodging tax. The question authorizes $404,598 in additional taxes in 2027 and whatever amounts the tax generates later, with no stated end date. Uses would include tourism promotion; recreation and visitor-related infrastructure; destination development and visitor-experience projects; tourism resiliency, emergency response and recovery related to events affecting visits; and administering and overseeing authorized lodging-tax programs. All revenue generated by the tax could be collected, retained and spent outside the stated constitutional and other legal limits.
yesMeans: Approve the county lodging-tax increase outside Cortez for the stated purposes and its revenue-limit exception.
noMeans: Do not approve this county lodging-tax increase or its proposed revenue-limit exception.
